title: The coffee counter
logline: Gully's counter in vol 7's summer: Gully's daughter, fifteen, working it; a girl at the counter with a zine; a crow on the sill. Wood on the end stool, drawn from behind. The town is somebody else's story this month.

panels.composition: Gully's counter in August, bright. Behind it: Gully's daughter, fifteen, apron, pulling a shot with her father's exact posture. On the customer side: a girl of sixteen or so, not local, with a stapled zine and an iced coffee, looking at the corkboard. On the sill: a crow. On the end stool, from behind, blue plaid: Wood. Gully himself in the doorway to the dock with a bucket, half out of frame. Everything the strip ever drew here, with other people in it.

characters.pose: in the dock doorway with a bucket, half out of frame

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a bright bait-and-espresso counter in August with a fifteen-year-old girl in an apron pulling an espresso shot, a teenage customer with a stapled zine and an iced coffee looking at a crowded corkboard, a crow on the windowsill, a graying man in blue plaid flannel seen from behind on the end stool, and a stocky older man with a bucket half out of frame in a doorway to a dock, no words
image.notes: The girl customer is vol 7's; draw her as a visitor, not a hero — no face detail that would pin her.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: Vol 7's summer from the end stool. Gully's girl pulls the shot.
